summary: On September 25, 2026, Mandiant released a report regarding continued mass exploitation of CVE-2026-35273 by the ShinyHunters group. TrendAI’s Zero Day Initiative first reported this CVE to Oracle on June 10, 2026, following an investigation I conducted with Minh Giang and Lucas Miller of TrendAI Research. Although Oracle issued a patch under a single CVE, we reported three distinct vulnerabilities across multiple PeopleSoft components. We are coordinating with Oracle to assign separate CVEs for each issue. In this blog post, we will walk through each of these vulnerabilities, starting with a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability. We will also review the validateClient method that Oracle introduced to allow PeopleSoft system administrators to restrict access to certain functionality. Spoiler alert: the SSRF allows attackers to make requests that satisfy this validation and access endpoints vulnerable to remote code execution (RCE). Overview There are two main components involved here, both served as individual Oracle WebLogic applications. The first, the PeopleSoft Environment Management Hub (PSEMHUB), is part of Oracle’s Environment Management Framework. This component implements the validateClient method, ensuring only trusted clients can reach PSEMHUB functionality. Because this is an internal management interface, it makes sense that Oracle would restrict access to its web endpoints. However, this also means it’s a prime target for attackers looking to pivot from their existing, low-privileged access. The second, the PeopleSoft Integration Gateway (PSIGW), contains functionality for exchanging messages between the PeopleSoft server and remote systems. This is accomplished using a set of Listening and Target Connectors. One such connector is the HttpListeningConnector , which translates data from inbound HTTP requests into the format supported by the specified Target Connector before routing the request to the desired URL. In this chain, attackers specify the HttpTargetConnector . The diagram below shows how an attacker like ShinyHunters can combine these vulnerabilities to compromise PeopleSoft systems. Notice that the attacker cannot simply hit the PSEMHUB functionality directly: Bug 1: PSIGW Server-Side Request Forgery (ZDI-CAN-31816) Now let’s take a look at how the PSIGW SSRF provides attackers with a foothold in the PeopleSoft application. An example malicious request to PSIGW shows just how powerful this is for an attacker. We control the URL to hit AND the full payload to send! At [1], the attacker sends a POST request to /PSIGW/HttpListeningConnector At [2], the HttpTargetConnector handler class is specified At [3], the target is PeopleSoft on the loopback interface at http://127.0.0.1:8000 , satisfying the validateClient logic At [4], the full POST request payload is specified in the Data field, to be forwarded to the target URL at [3] The HttpTargetConnector handler appears below. Note there is no validation to ensure this traffic is legitimate and bound for a valid target. I've done my best to pull out the important parts of this 800+-line function. If you want a fun side quest, go decompile this for yourself and check it out. I hope you like spaghetti! At [1], retrieve the target URL from the attacker's request At [2], create an httpObj using the URL from [1] At [3], retrieve the HTTP method (POST) and apply it to the httpObj from [2] At [4], send the content data seen in the Data tag of the network request. This content is sent as-is using the HTTP parameters configured in the httpObj To fully understand why this SSRF is valuable, here is the validateClient method I mentioned earlier: At [1] and [2], the validateClient method pulls the hostname and IP of the requesting client At [3], a file path is built to the /envmetadata/config/allowedhosts.properties file, which contains the list of hosts allowed to access functionality protected by validateClient At [4], the server checks if the allowedList set contains any entries. The first time this path is hit, the set is empty, so execution continues into the client list refresh block At [5], that allowedhosts.properties file is read and iterated over At [6] and [7], each allowed host is added to the allowedList set, including the default localhost entry alongside the server's resolved hostname and IP address At [8] and [9], if the requesting host is found in the allowedList set, validateClient returns true We can see the localhost entry in the default allowedhosts.properties that ships with PeopleSoft: While this solution does restrict access, an attacker on any trusted host can still reach PSEMHUB. Because Oracle allows localhost by default, the PSIGW SSRF provides exactly that access. Bug 2: PSEMHUB External Control of File Path (ZDI-CAN-31818) Now that the attacker can make requests to the PSEMHUB endpoints using the PSIGW SSRF, let's see how they can turn that into RCE. The first path to code execution uses an External Control of File Path vulnerability in the ExecuteProcessActivityCommand handler, which is designed to allow remote clients to write log entries to the PeopleSoft server’s filesystem. However, callers of the command control both the file contents AND the absolute file path on disk to which that content is written. Here’s an example of the request made to PSEMHUB. Note that, in practice, each parameter value is a form-encoded serialized Java object. For clarity, I’ve decoded and formatted it here: At [1], we see the request is being made to PSEMHUB’s central routing hub At [2], note that the request is made to the loopback address 127.0.0.1. Since this request originates from localhost, the validateClient check is satisfied At [3], the web shell contents are specified in the m_line parameter At [4], the absolute path where the contents will be written is specified in the m_targetFile parameter Looking at the handler for this request, we can see that no validation is performed to ensure that m_targetFile points to a legitimate log directory: By writing this shell to the PSEMHUB WAR path, the attacker achieves immediate remote code execution in the context of the PeopleSoft service account. Here's how those bugs look when chained together: Bug 3: PSEMHUB Deserialization of Untrusted Data (ZDI-CAN-31817) Using any file write primitive (like the ExecuteProcessActivityCommand seen above), an attacker can write a malicious XML file inside the [docroot]/envmetadata/data/environment/ directory. When the PSEMHUB HubServlet class initializes next (after a system or service restart, for example), it triggers a code flow that ultimately deserializes this XML file. Because this vector does not require writing a JSP web shell, it is less likely to be noticed by standard detection methods. Specifically, on initialization, the PSEMHUB HubServlet class calls startServerPeer in the com.peoplesoft.pt.environmentmanagement.hub.Server class: At [1], HubMBeanPersistance.getInstance() is called, which triggers the private constructor for that class At [2], env_dir_path is set to <context_root>/envmetadata/data/environment/ , which contains the malicious XML file placed by the attacker At [3], all files from this folder are loaded into a list variable fl At [4] and [5], the absolute path for each file in that directory is built At [6], XMLDecoder is instantiated for each file At [7], the content of the malicious XML placed by the attacker is deserialized Java's XMLDecoder instantiates and configures the objects described in the XML during parsing, so the attacker's payload executes before the cast to Environment throws an exception. Conclusion The combination of the powerful PSIGW Server-Side Request Forgery primitive alongside the decision to allow access to PSEMHUB via the loopback address by default renders the validateClient protection ineffective. Attackers can combine these vulnerabilities to compromise affected instances of PeopleSoft. The impact of SSRFs can sometimes be overlooked, especially if they have no standalone information disclosure impact. Under the right circumstances, however, the humble SSRF can open the door for complete compromise. You can find me on Twitter at @bobbygould5 , and follow the team on Twitter , Mastodon , LinkedIn , or Bluesky for the latest in exploit techniques and security patches.

summary: CISA has added two new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog , based on evidence of active exploitation. CVE-2026-48356 Adobe Commerce and Magento Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type Vulnerability CVE-2026-111497 Google Brotli Unchecked Return Value Vulnerability These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities . CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria . Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form . Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

Mitigation For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend blocking unauthorized access by using a firewall, virtual private network (VPN), etc. and allowing remote login only to administrator when internet access is required, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability. Mitigation For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend restricting physical access to the PC with the affected product installed and the network to which the PC is connected, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability. Mitigation For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend preventing the user from clicking on web links in emails from untrusted sources, or from opening attachments in untrusted emails, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability. Mitigation For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend using the PCs with the affected product installed in the LAN and blocking access from untrusted networks and hosts through firewalls, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability. Mitigation For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend blocking unauthorized access by using a firewall, virtual private network (VPN), etc. when internet access is required, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability. Mitigation For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend installing anti-virus software on the PC with the affected product installed, as well as on any PCs that can access it, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability. Recommended Practices CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet . Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Security researchers have reported exploitation attempts surrounding the October 21 emergency security release, including activity observed before public disclosure, while VulnCheck documented automated scanning and an unsuccessful attempt to deploy a web shell through PHP session-handling functionality. With millions of internet-facing PHP deployments potentially exposed and a substantial proportion running unsupported versions, organizations face an urgent need to remediate vulnerable systems and investigate suspicious activity preceding the security release.

summary: Overview On October 21, 2026, the Node.js Project published a security advisory for CVE-2026-111497 , an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js. The vulnerability affects the Node.js 26.x , 24.x , and 22.x release lines. Node.js rates the issue High, while Google, the CVE Numbering Authority (CNA), gives it a critical CVSSv4 score of 9.2 . An attacker who can supply Brotli data that an application decompresses with node:zlib can corrupt process memory. According to Node.js, this corruption can lead to a process crash, disclosure of sensitive process memory, or remote code execution. Exposure therefore depends on whether an application passes attacker-controlled compressed data to the affected decoder. On October 27, 2026, CVE-2026-111497 was added to the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency's (CISA) list of known exploited vulnerabilities (KEV), based on evidence of active exploitation. Given the vulnerability's potential to disclose memory or enable remote code execution (RCE), Rapid7 recommends that organizations prioritize remediation. Technical overview CVE-2026-111497 is classified as an out-of-bounds write ( CWE-787 ) and an unchecked return value ( CWE-252 ). Per the vendor advisory, the decoder handled an invalid Brotli block switch as a temporary need for more input instead of a permanent format error. The streaming decoder then continued appending input bytes to an eight-byte internal buffer, allowing malformed input to write beyond the buffer and corrupt process memory. The vulnerability originates in Google Brotli, which the affected Node.js release lines bundle as a dependency. The CVE record identifies affected upstream Brotli ranges on all platforms as versions 1.0.3 before 1.0.10 , 1.1.0 before 1.1.1 , and 1.2.0 before 1.2.1 . The Node.js Project remediated its bundled decoder in the fixed Node.js releases listed below. Because CVE-2026-111497 affects the upstream Google Brotli decoder, its reach is not limited to Node.js. Vendor and project advisories have also identified affected implementations in Bun , Python's Brotli and brotlicffi packages, .NET , Envoy and Istio , brotli4j , and operating-system packages . Affected versions, default exposure, and remediation vary by product; the presence of an affected decoder does not by itself establish exposure unless an application processes attacker-controlled Brotli data. Organizations should consult the relevant downstream vendor or distribution advisories to identify affected versions, assess exposure, and determine appropriate remediation. Mitigation guidance Vendor-supplied security updates are available to remediate CVE-2026-111497. Organizations running an affected Node.js release should upgrade on an urgent basis, outside of normal patch cycles: Node.js 22.x releases before 22.23.4 are affected; upgrade to 22.23.4 or later. Node.js 24.x releases before 24.22.1 are affected; upgrade to 24.22.1 or later. Node.js 26.x releases before 26.12.1 are affected; upgrade to 26.12.1 or later. The vendor states that end-of-life Node.js release lines should also be treated as affected when a security release occurs. Organizations using an end-of-life release should migrate to a supported, fixed release line. Node.js has not published a vendor-supported workaround; if an immediate upgrade is not possible, Rapid7 recommends restricting or disabling application paths that decompress untrusted Brotli data as a temporary exposure-reduction measure. For the latest mitigation guidance, please refer to the Node.js security advisory . Rapid7 customers Exposure Command, Vulnerability Management, and Nexpose Exposure Command, Vulnerability Management, and Nexpose customers can assess exposure to CVE-2026-111497 with an authenticated vulnerability check for Linux, macOS, and Windows, available in the October 26 content release. Updates October 26, 2026 : Initial publication. October 26, 2026 : Updated the Exposure Command, Vulnerability Management, and Nexpose section to reflect coverage availability. October 27, 2026 : Updated Overview to add a reference to CVE-2026-111497 being added to the CISA KEV list.

summary: CISA has added two new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog and updated the PHP Alert, Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP Require Immediate Patching : CVE-2026-109618 – PHP Memory Corruption Vulnerability CVE-2026-109619 – PHP Stale Internal Request-State Vulnerability These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities . CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria . Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form . Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

summary:
Between October 17 and October 20, 2026, a critical security compromise involving Certificate Authorities that are managed by eMudhra was uncovered. A security researcher demonstrated that the private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were fundamentally broken due to an unprecedented error in their Key Generation Ceremony (KGC) in April 2025. This allows anyone to brute-force acquire these private keys within seconds. For more information, see eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise and the Cisco Talos blog post Compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates . For information about Splunk products and offerings, see Compromised eMudhra Intermediate Certificate Authorities on Splunk Products - October 2026 . Important: If a product is not listed within this advisory, Cisco's review indicates that the product is not affected by this vulnerability. This advisory will be updated as additional information becomes available. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-emudhra-info-ScS22A1r
Security Impact Rating: Informational

summary: CISA has added one new vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog , based on evidence of active exploitation. CVE-2026-110447 Collabora Online – Built-in CODE Server OS Command Injection Vulnerability This type of vulnerability is a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and poses significant risks to the federal enterprise. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities . CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria . Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form . Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

summary:
Multiple Cisco products are affected by a vulnerability in the Snort 3 SMTP MIME Decoder that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the Snort 3 Detection Engine to restart. This vulnerability is due to a lack of error checking when the MIME fields of the SMTP header are parsed. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted SMTP packets through an established connection to be parsed by Snort 3. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause a denial of service (DoS) condition when the Snort 3 Detection Engine unexpectedly restarts. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-snort3-mime-vulns-bkXjcKkt This advisory is part of a group of advisories. For a complete list of the advisories and links to them, see Cisco Advance Notification for Publication of October 21, 2026, Security Advisories . summary:
Multiple Cisco products are affected by a vulnerability in the generic routing encapsulation (GRE) tunnel decapsulation feature of the Snort 3 Detection Engine that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause an unexpected restart of the Snort 3 Detection Engine. This vulnerability is due to improper handling of nested GRE traffic. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted GRE payload through an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to trigger an unexpected reload of the Snort 3 Detection Engine, resulting in either a bypass or denial of service (DoS) condition, depending on device configuration. For more information, see the Details section of this advisory. The Snort 3 Detection Engine will restart automatically. No manual intervention is required. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-snort3-gre-JNpMHrTv This advisory is part of a group of advisories. summary:
Multiple Cisco products are affected by a vulnerability in the Snort 3 Detection Engine that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the detection engine to unexpectedly restart, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition. The vulnerability is due to a flaw in logic handling when General Packet Radio Service (GPRS) Tunneling Protocol (GTP) extension headers are processed within the codec. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted, fragmented UDP datagram that contains these headers to the Snort 3 Detection Engine of an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the detection engine to enter an infinite loop, resulting in a DoS condition. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are workarounds that address this vulnerability. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-snort3-gtpcodec-dos-Rmecfepz This advisory is part of a group of advisories. summary:

summary: View CSAF Summary .NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API contains multiple vulnerabilities that could allow an attacker to obtain sensitive information or write arbitrary files outside the intended download directory. Siemens has released a new version for .NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API and recommends to update to the latest version. The following versions of Siemens SIMATIC S7 Webserver API are affected: .NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API vers:intdot/<3.3.61, vers:intdot/<3.3.62 (CVE-2026-85114, CVE-2026-85115) CVSS Vendor Equipment v3 7.5 Siemens .NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API 2 Vulnerabilities Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal'), Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information Background Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide Company Headquarters Location: Germany Vulnerabilities Expand All + CVE-2026-85114 Affected applications do not properly validate filenames received from remote servers during ticket downloads. This could allow an attacker who can manipulate the ticket response to write arbitrary files outside the intended download directory and, when overwriting is enabled, replace existing files accessible to the application. Read More 1 Affected Product .NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API < V3.3.61 Product Status: known_affected Remediations Vendor fix Update to V3.3.61 or later version Additional Metrics Relevant CWE: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String 3.1 7.5 HIGH CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N View CVE Details CVE-2026-85115 Affected applications do not properly redact PLC restore passwords from HTTP error exception messages. This could allow an attacker with access to logs or other diagnostic output to obtain the plaintext restore password and potentially perform unauthorized operations on the PLC. Read More 2 Affected Products .NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API < V3.3.61 Product Status: known_affected Remediations .NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API < V3.3.62 Product Status: known_affected Remediations Vendor fix Update to V3.3.62 or later version Additional Metrics Relevant CWE: CWE-209 Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String 3.1 5.5 MEDIUM CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N View CVE Details Acknowledgments Siemens ProductCERT reported these vulnerabilities to CISA. General Recommendations As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity Additional Resources For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisories Terms of Use The use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use. Recommended Practices CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet . Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices. CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures. CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics . Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies . CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets . Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies . Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents. Advisory Conversion Disclaimer This ICSA is a verbatim republication of Siemens ProductCERT SSA-390352 from a direct conversion of the vendor's Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) advisory. This is republished to CISA's website as a means of increasing visibility and is provided "as-is" for informational purposes only. CISA is not responsible for the editorial or technical accuracy of republished advisories and provides no warranties of any kind regarding any information contained within this advisory. Further, CISA does not endorse any commercial product or service. Please contact Siemens ProductCERT directly for any questions regarding this advisory. General Recommendations As a general security measure Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to affected products with appropriate mechanisms. It is advised to follow recommended security practices in order to run the devices in a protected IT environment. Additional Resources For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisories Terms of Use The use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use. Recommended Practices CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet . Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices. CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures. CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics . Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies . CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets . Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies . Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents. An authenticated user with the required privileges can define a dashboard containing a malicious payload, or a victim can be socially engineered into importing a malicious dashboard. A remote authenticated user with limited privileges can view a limited subset of the available entries in the Credentials Manager. summary: View CSAF Summary The Industrial Edge App Publisher contains a vulnerability chain involving improper certificate validation and the rendering of unescaped data from backend responses. Siemens has released an update for the Industrial Edge App Publisher and recommends to update to the latest version. This allows an attacker to intercept and relay communication (Man-in-the-Middle attack) and to spoof a trusted entity by interfering in the communication path between the client and the intended server. General Recommendations As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends protecting network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends configuring the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security ( https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-securit y), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Recommended Practices CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the exploitation risk of this vulnerability. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, and ensure they are not accessible from the internet. Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolate them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most recent version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as its connected devices. CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures. Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents. summary: View CSAF Summary Multiple SIMATIC WinCC versions are affected by a database privilege escalation vulnerability that could allow an authenticated user with access to the database to execute commands on the underlying host system. Siemens has released new versions for several affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions. Siemens is preparing further fixes and recommends mitigations for products where fixes are not or not yet available. The following versions of Siemens WinCC are affected: SIMATIC WinCC V7.5 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-59241) SIMATIC WinCC V8.0 vers:intdot/<8.0.0.11 (CVE-2026-59241) SIMATIC WinCC V8.1 vers:intdot/<8.1.7 (CVE-2026-59241) CVSS Vendor Equipment v3 8.8 Siemens SIMATIC WinCC V7.5 1 Vulnerability Incorrect Privilege Assignment Background Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide Company Headquarters Location: Germany Vulnerabilities CVE-2026-59241 The affected application does not sufficiently restrict the permissions assigned to a database role. This could allow an authenticated remote attacker with database access to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary commands on the host system where SIMATIC WinCC is installed, potentially leading to a compromise of the system. General Recommendations As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity Additional Resources For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisories Terms of Use The use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use. Recommended Practices CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet . Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices. CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures. CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics . Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies . CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets . Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies . Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents. summary: View CSAF Summary The products listed below contain an out-of-bounds read vulnerability that could allow an attacker to cause abnormal product behavior, instability, or denial of service. Siemens has released a new version for Capital Embedded AR Classic R20-11 and recommends updating to the latest version. Siemens is preparing further fix versions and recommends specific countermeasures for products where fixes are not, or not yet available. The following versions of Siemens Capital Embedded AR Classic are affected: Capital Embedded AR Classic 431-422 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-89208) Capital Embedded AR Classic R20-11 vers:intdot/<2303 (CVE-2026-89208) CVSS Vendor Equipment v3 5.3 Siemens Capital Embedded AR Classic 431-422 1 Vulnerability Out-of-bounds Read Background Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide Company Headquarters Location: Germany Vulnerabilities CVE-2026-89208 The affected product does not properly validate input bounds before accessing packet data. summary: View CSAF Summary The products listed below contain a vulnerability that could allow an attacker to boot an operating system or UEFI application signed with that test key, bypassing UEFI Secure Boot protections even when Secure Boot is enabled. Siemens has released new versions for the affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions. The following versions of Siemens SIMATIC IPCs are affected: SIMATIC IPC BX-21A vers:intdot/<31.01.13 (CVE-2026-72895) SIMATIC IPC RW-543A vers:intdot/<1.1.4 (CVE-2026-72895) SIMATIC IPC227G / IPC277G / IPC277G PRO / IPC327G / IPC377G vers:intdot/<28.01.15 (CVE-2026-72895) CVSS Vendor Equipment v3 7.7 Siemens SIMATIC IPC BX-21A 1 Vulnerability Use of Default Cryptographic Key Background Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide Company Headquarters Location: Germany Vulnerabilities CVE-2026-72895 A BIOS vendor test key is present in the UEFI Secure Boot key database. This could allow a local attacker with physical or administrative access to the device to boot an operating system or UEFI application signed with that test key, bypassing UEFI Secure Boot protections even when Secure Boot is enabled, potentially leading to a full loss of confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the device. Note: Loading default settings will restore the test key, so upgrading remains recommended. General Recommendations As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Recommended Practices CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet . Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. vulnerabilities to CISA. General Recommendations As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity Additional Resources For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisories Terms of Use The use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use. Recommended Practices CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet . Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices. CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures. CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics . Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies . CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets . Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies . Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents. Recommended Practices CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet . Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents. summary: Multiple vulnerabilities have been discovered in PHP, the most severe of which could allow for remote code execution. PHP is a widely-used, open-source server-side scripting language designed primarily for web development. All PHP installations serving web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed are considered at risk. Successful exploitation of the most severe of these vulnerabilities could allow for unauthenticated remote code execution in the context of the affected service account. Depending on the privileges associated with the service account, an attacker could then install programs; view, change, or delete data; or create new accounts with full user rights. Services whose accounts are configured to have less rights on the system could be less impacted than those who operate with administrative user rights.

summary:
A vulnerability in Cisco Expressway Series could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to obtain sensitive information from an affected device. This vulnerability is due to insufficient authorization checks of HTTP requests during Mobile and Remote Access (MRA) provisioning. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted URL request to an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to access sensitive information that they would otherwise not have authorization to access. Note: Cisco Expressway Series refers to Cisco Expressway Core (Expressway-C) devices and Cisco Expressway Edge (Expressway-E) devices. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-expressway-inf-disc-vvYqgSTS This advisory is part of a group of advisories. summary:
A vulnerability in the IPv4 packet processing functionality of Cisco IOS XR Software that affects Cisco ASR 9000 and 9900 Series Aggregation Services Routers as well as Cisco ASR 9902 and 9903 Compact High-Performance Routers could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause network processor (NP) errors, resulting in a line card reset or shutdown and a denial of service (DoS) condition. This vulnerability is due to the incorrect handling of crafted IPv4 packets that are received on an affected line card interface and processed as for-us traffic. The issue can result in an NP reset, causing traffic loss on the affected line card while it recovers. Under repeated reset conditions, the network processor may enter a persistent shutdown state, in which case an explicit line card reload may be required to restore traffic. The vulnerability is within the IPv4 packet-processing path. Transit IPv4 traffic does not trigger this issue and IPv6 traffic cannot trigger it. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-asr9k-tUyxcyXN
Security Impact Rating: High
CVE: CVE-2026-76505

summary:
A vulnerability in the database service feature of Cisco Expressway Series could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker with network access to a Cisco Expressway device to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root . This vulnerability is due to the use of persistent cookies. Additionally, there is insufficient validation of client certificates when the TLS Verify Mode is set to Enabled for clustering, which means that client certificates are not validated. An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root on the underlying operating system of an affected device. Note: Cisco Expressway Series refers to Cisco Expressway Core (Expressway-C) devices and Cisco Expressway Edge (Expressway-E) devices. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-vcs-static-cred-hr7EWZ8t This advisory is part of a group of advisories. For a complete list of the advisories and links to them, see Cisco Advance Notification for Publication of October 21, 2026, Security Advisories . In addition, for further documentation of improvements and fixes in Cisco Expressway Series see Cisco Expressway Series Security Hardening Release: October 2026 .

summary:
A vulnerability in the control channel socket implementation of Open Source Snort 3 could allow an authenticated, local attacker with low privileges to execute arbitrary commands as the Snort 3 process user. This vulnerability is due to a lack of authentication when a local user connects to the Snort control channel socket. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the Snort 3 control channel socket as a local user. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary commands as well as read and write Snort 3 process memory. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-opensrc-snort3-2fXGJPfe This advisory is part of a group of advisories. summary:
A vulnerability in the interprocess communication (IPC) channel of the Secure Firewall Posture module in Cisco Secure Client could allow an authenticated, local attacker to elevate privileges on an affected device. This vulnerability is due to insufficient validation of user-supplied input. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a series of crafted IPC messages to a local socket. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to perform limited file write operations on the filesystem with SYSTEM or root privileges. Although this vulnerability affects the Secure Firewall Posture module in Cisco Secure Client on Windows, macOS, and Linux operating systems, this vulnerability could be used to obtain full root privileges on macOS and Linux. For that reason Cisco has assigned this security advisory a Security Impact Rating (SIR) of High rather than Medium as the score indicates. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-sec-client-priv-esc-muF8eZdm
Security Impact Rating: High

summary: Overview On October 21, 2026, the PHP project announced security releases for two critical vulnerabilities in PHP. CVE-2026-109618 can corrupt memory during out-of-memory (OOM) handling, while CVE-2026-109619 is a use-after-free flaw involving state retained between requests. Both have a CVSSv4 score of 9.2 and both can allow for unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) with the web worker's privileges. CVE CVSSv4 Description CVE-2026-109618 9.2 (Critical) RCE via OOM corruption CVE-2026-109619 9.2 (Critical) RCE via stale global state All installations serving web requests are at risk, including PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed. The vendor considers mod_php the highest risk because exploitation can succeed before any application code runs. The advisories report that a successful RCE exploit was developed during research, including achieving RCE against Apache mod_php and PHP-FPM through different attack paths. As of October 21, 2026, there are multiple indications that this research is being independently reproduced, and a viable exploit is expected to be made public soon. Due to the extremely high deployment of PHP based web applications, exploitation in-the-wild is expected. Rapid7 recommends updating affected installations on an emergency basis, outside of normal patch cycles. Multiple public proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 are now available. Rapid7 researchers have reviewed these and observe that each demonstrates RCE only against a specific combination of operating system, PHP version, and web server, and none appears to be broadly reliable. Rapid7’s own research supports this. Our attempts so far have produced a working exploit only under narrow lab conditions, and exploitation depends on assumptions that are unlikely to hold on internet-facing instances. We are continuing to investigate approaches that could improve portability, but have not yet developed a reliable, general-purpose exploit. Rapid7 has not observed exploitation in the wild, though there are multiple reports of exploitation attempts, which is expected for a vulnerability of this profile. The situation is evolving quickly, and a more portable exploit technique could emerge at any time. The current difficulty of reliable exploitation should be treated as a window to patch rather than a reason to delay, and Rapid7 continues to recommend updating affected installations on an emergency basis. Update #1 : On October 26, 2026, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 were added to the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency's (CISA) list of known exploited vulnerabilities (KEV) , based on evidence of active exploitation. CISA set the remediation due date to October 29, 2026, for affected Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies and directs them to follow the associated BOD 26-04 forensic triage requirements . Rapid7 continues to recommend updating affected installations on an emergency basis and investigating for prior compromise. Technical overview CVE-2026-109618: Memory corruption during OOM handling According to the OOM advisory , PHP can abruptly abandon request processing when a memory allocation fails. If internal request data is only partly initialized, that exit can leave invalid data for request cleanup to use. Crafted multipart requests, used for forms and file uploads, can exhaust memory even when their size appears to meet PHP's configured limits. Application operations that allocate memory in response to attacker input can also trigger OOM. Apache mod_php runs cleanup even when request startup fails, enabling the demonstrated attack before application code executes. The advisory reports RCE over HTTP with default PHP input and memory limits, including multi-worker prefork deployments. PHP-FPM terminates a worker when startup fails, preventing that particular sequence. Source analysis supports FPM susceptibility after successful startup, but the advisory reports no complete FPM exploit for this CVE. Exploit portability and reliability depend on the PHP build, extensions, frontend behavior, and memory layout. CVE-2026-109619: Use after free across requests PHP can reuse a worker process to handle multiple HTTP requests. The stale-state advisory describes internal state that still points to memory freed at the end of an earlier request. A later request handled by the same worker can access that stale value before normal initialization clears it. Fatal errors, including memory exhaustion and execution timeouts, can interrupt state cleanup; some nonfatal diagnostics during shutdown can also repopulate error state after it was reset. The advisory confirms RCE against mod_php through PHP 8.5's fatal error backtrace feature, when fatal_error_backtraces is enabled (the default), where a later initialization diagnostic accesses stale backtrace state. It also confirms session lifecycle RCE against mod_php and FPM. Session upload progress, PHP's upload-tracking feature, is enabled by default and can act as an early consumer of stale session or decoder state before normal initialization; reaching this consumer does not itself require an application call to session_start() . The validated FPM session path requires a suitable application operation to leave state behind after successful startup, followed by a fatal error and another request that consumes the stale state through session upload progress. Both requests must reach the same worker. Multiple workers and worker recycling can reduce success per request, but do not eliminate the condition. Mitigation guidance PHP has released fixes for both vulnerabilities. Organizations should prioritize updating to the appropriate fixed release or a vendor package containing both complete patches. The PHP advisories list these affected and fixed versions: PHP 8.2 releases before 8.2.35: Update to 8.2.35 PHP 8.3 releases before 8.3.36: Update to 8.3.36 PHP 8.4 releases before 8.4.27: Update to 8.4.27 PHP 8.5 releases before 8.5.12: Update to 8.5.12 Linux distributions and long-term support vendors received patches in advance; check your vendor for updated packages. PHP 8.1 and older no longer receive routine upstream updates. For this incident, PHP has supplied limited source backports for PHP 7.4 , 8.0 , and 8.1 . Organizations running older branches should obtain a vendor fix, use the source backports described in the PHP announcement , or upgrade to a supported version. PHP also warns that rpms.remirepo.net will not have updates on October 21, 2026, and urges its users to switch to distribution packages or build from source. Note that an update containing both complete fixes is the only complete remediation. PHP's temporary configuration measures reduce exposure to specific paths and require careful deployment: For the OOM issue, enforce memory_limit=-1 administratively, such as through FPM pool or Apache configuration that applications cannot override. This disables PHP's per-request memory cap and removes the predictable PHP-limit failure used by the confirmed exploit. An underlying allocation failure can still reach the vulnerable path. Restart every worker and verify that no pool, directory, or application setting restores a finite limit. For the session lifecycle path, set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 in php.ini , an FPM pool, or server configuration that applies before request parsing, then restart every worker. Application-level ini_set() and FPM .user.ini are too late. This addresses the confirmed session paths only. On PHP 8.5, set fatal_error_backtraces=0 administratively and restart every worker. This addresses the confirmed fatal backtrace path only; other retained state remains a concern. Disabling PHP's memory cap makes independent resource controls particularly important. PHP recommends post_max_size=8M where uploads are unnecessary or post_max_size=32M where they are needed, with upload_max_filesize below that limit. At the frontend, bound decoded request size, input and multipart counts, headers per part, and nesting depth, including requests without a usable Content-Length . If the application does not use multipart data, block those requests before they reach PHP. Container or cgroup memory limits are also incomplete: allocation failures remain possible, and enforcement can kill the master process and all workers unless workers are isolated. Do not substitute RLIMIT_AS or RLIMIT_DATA , which can trigger the vulnerable allocation-failure path. For stale-state exposure, correct invalid or deprecated per-request settings and attacker-reachable fatal errors or timeouts. Hiding diagnostics through error_reporting , display_errors , log_errors , or @ does not prevent stale-state access. The absence of relevant log entries is not proof that an installation is safe. For the latest mitigation guidance, refer to PHP's OOM corruption advisory and stale global state advisory . Rapid7 customers To learn how to use Rapid7 capabilities to find systems affected by these vulnerabilities and for answers to common questions, read the PHP2Shell documentation . For Rapid7 Customers with questions regarding Rapid7 products and their usage of PHP please consult this page. Exposure Command, Vulnerability Management, and Nexpose Exposure Command, Vulnerability Management, and Nexpose customers can assess exposure to CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 with remote unauthenticated vulnerability checks, available in a dedicated release that followed the regular October 21 content release. Rapid7 has also released authenticated scan checks for both the Scan Engine and the Agent for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 as part of the October 22 content release. Authenticated, package-based checks are now available for a variety of Linux distributions. These checks evaluate installed distribution packages, so they can recognize backported fixes that keep the original upstream PHP version number. Run an authenticated scan with this content release to use them. For the full list of checks and supported distribution versions, read Rapid7’s PHP2Shell documentation , where package-based coverage for other distributions will be added as their fixes are published. In a dedicated October 23 content release following the regular release, Rapid7 has released coverage for CVE-2026-115560, published on October 23 by the PHP Foundation. A mitigation technique is available, but no patch has yet been published. Exploitation of CVE-2026-115560 relies on non-standard configuration. Current scope for authenticated coverage: Windows, macOS and Linux. Remote unauthenticated coverage provides coverage regardless of web-server OS. Velociraptor A Velociraptor Artifact Generic.Applications.PHPInventory is available to inventory PHP installations on Windows, Linux and macOS for remediation scoping. This artifact allows for the collection of package versions, common binary and module paths, and running PHP processes. Updates October 21, 2026: Initial publication. October 21, 2026: Updated to reflect availability of vulnerability checks. October 22, 2026 : Updated the Overview section to include Rapid7’s findings on a PoC and the Rapid7 Customers section to include a link to the FAQ documentation. October 23, 2026 : Updated the Exposure Command, Vulnerability Management, and Nexpose section to describe authenticated coverage, Linux distro backported coverage, and more. October 27, 2026 : Updated the Overview to note that CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 were added to the CISA KEV catalog. Updated Rapid7 customers section to reflect added Windows support.

summary: On 20 October 2026, the PHP project announced an upcoming security release addressing two critical vulnerabilities in PHP. The PHP team released the fixes today, 21 October 2026 at 13:30 UTC, in PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Both vulnerabilities can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. Technical details are now being discussed publicly, and initial proofs of concept (PoCs) have begun to circulate. This raises the likelihood that attackers are already exploiting the vulnerabilities. [New] On 23 October, PHP disclosed a new RCE vulnerability. However, it affects only web applications configured in an unusual way, and PHP considers it an unlikely risk. PHP will not issue an out-of-band release for this vulnerability. Instead, organisations are advised to apply mitigation to fully protect from this RCE vector. CERT-EU advises organisations to patch affected assets immediately. Where that is not feasible, organisations should consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is applied and verified.

summary: Three days is the average time between a high-severity vulnerability becoming public and its exploitation, according to the latest Quarterly Threat Landscape Report from Rapid7. And 71% of the exploitation tracked in Q3 occurred within the first seven days. For security teams already managing growing vulnerability backlogs, this creates a difficult question: How do you reduce exposure when attackers can exploit vulnerabilities before your next patching window? Rapid7's Q3 2026 research brings together vulnerability intelligence, ransomware activity, APT tracking, and underground forum intelligence to show where attacker activity is concentrated. The exploitation window has narrowed, big time Rapid7 tracked 43 newly exploited high- and critical-severity vulnerabilities this quarter, down 7% from Q2 but still 19% higher than the same period last year. The number of newly exploited vulnerabilities isn't growing at the same rate as disclosures. The more pressing concern is how quickly attackers exploit the vulnerabilities they choose. On average, exploitation occurred just three days after public disclosure. The report also found that 80% of tracked exploitation occurred within 14 days and 90% within 30 days. That timeline creates a serious challenge for organizations relying on fixed remediation schedules. It also reinforces the need to distinguish between vulnerabilities that are theoretically severe and those that pose an immediate, exploitable risk. The report examines the exploitation timeline in greater detail, including the vulnerability characteristics that make certain exposures particularly attractive to attackers. Attackers are exploiting vulnerabilities that require no interaction Q3's vulnerability data reveals another concerning pattern: Of the 43 newly exploited high- and critical-severity vulnerabilities tracked, 34 (79%) required no authentication or user interaction. This provides attackers a potential path into exposed systems, no stolen credentials or malicious content interaction necessary. An internet-facing service with an exploitable vulnerability may require immediate attention, particularly when an attacker can reach it without authenticating. This makes attack surface visibility and contextual prioritization essential. Security teams need to understand which systems are externally accessible, which vulnerabilities are actively exploited, and whether existing controls can prevent or limit compromise. A CVSS score alone won’t give you the answers. The report explores the characteristics of exploited vulnerabilities and why understanding reachability is critical to reducing risk. AI is taking on a more operational role in attacks In Q3, 8% of the threat reporting tracked by Rapid7 cited AI as an operational component. The research identifies a shift from using AI primarily to help draft content or code toward supporting tactical decisions and execution within attack campaigns. In the documented cases, human operators continued to select targets and determine objectives, but relied on AI assistance for technique selection, target assessment, and adapting when an attack step failed. The report also examines how threat actors split malicious objectives across multiple AI sessions to evade provider safeguards. There are serious implications for detection in these findings. AI-enabled attacks also reinforce the value of monitoring and quickly adapting to attacker behavior rather than relying exclusively on known malware signatures or threat actor identities. The report provides additional context on how AI appeared in tracked campaigns and what defenders should monitor. The next step: Prioritize exposure before attackers exploit it Q3's findings reveal a challenge that vulnerability counts alone can’t explain. Attackers exploited 43 newly tracked vulnerabilities this quarter, yet the average exploitation window was just three days. Meanwhile, underground forum monitoring identified 41 posts advertising RDP or network access, demonstrating continued interest in selling access to compromised environments. Security teams must account for both the vulnerabilities attackers can exploit directly and the access they can obtain through other means. Start by identifying externally accessible assets and the vulnerabilities affecting them. Prioritize known exploitation, unauthenticated access paths, and systems supporting critical business functions. Where immediate remediation isn't possible, assess compensating controls and detection coverage. The latest Rapid7 Quarterly Threat Landscape Report brings together vulnerability research, ransomware intelligence, nation-state activity, and dark web monitoring to help security teams understand where threats are concentrated and what to address first. Download and read it now .

summary: Update October 26, 2026: CISA has updated this Alert to reflect the addition of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Oct. 26, 2026. Update October 23, 2026 : CISA has updated this Alert to: (1) provide a SIGMA detection rule to help identify potentially suspicious activity; (2) incorporate partner resources; and (3) reinforce existing mitigation guidance. Purpose CISA strongly urges organizations to immediately patch the recently disclosed critical vulnerabilities in PHP, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 . These vulnerabilities, known as “php2shell,” allow for unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP. The vulnerabilities affect all PHP installations serving web requests, including Apache with mod_php ( Note : PHP considers this highest risk), PHP-FPM, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. Organizations should immediately update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35 to fix these vulnerabilities. CISA added CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to its KEV Catalog on Oct. 26, 2026. Actions to take CISA urges organizations to take the following actions: Identify and inventory systems running any version of PHP across your organization. PHP is often a component of other software and prevalence may not be directly observable. Apply the patch immediately, prioritizing internet-facing systems. Organizations that cannot update immediately, or that continue to use PHP 8.1 or earlier unsupported versions, should take PHP-based systems offline until they can be patched or updated. A web application firewall may provide some protection until systems are updated or patched. Review the official PHP security advisory for guidance on patching. Monitor for suspicious activity, including PHP worker processes launching shells or downloading tools.
